html:
The oil company founded in 1870 in Cleveland, Ohio, by John D. Rockefeller and his partners. It grew into the most famous monopoly in American history.

Its main product at first was kerosene for lamps. Standard Oil cut costs, made secret deals with railroads for cheap freight, and bought out or crushed rivals. By about 1880 it controlled some 90 per cent of oil refining in the United States. In 1882 its many firms were joined in a trust. Its kerosene was sold across the world, in competition with Branobel in Russia and later Royal Dutch.

Rockefeller became the richest man of his time. The journalist Ida Tarbell exposed the company's methods in 1902 to 1904. The government sued under the Sherman Antitrust Act, and in 1911 the Supreme Court ordered it broken into 34 companies.

The pieces grew into giants of their own: Standard Oil of New Jersey became Exxon, of New York became Mobil, and of California became Chevron.
sum: The oil company founded in 1870 in Cleveland, Ohio, by John D. Rockefeller and his partners. It grew into the most famous monopoly in American history.
